c.tagline: Romeo and Juliet's romantic Roman city.

emergency.note: 112 is the universal EU number; 113 police and 118 ambulance also work, with English often available.

avoid.reason: Pickpockets target crowds at the Arena, Piazza Bra and Juliet's House, and the Porta Nuova station area feels sketchy late at night.

hood_desc: Centro Storico (Citta Antica) is the walkable UNESCO heart of Verona, home to the Roman Arena, Piazza Bra, Piazza delle Erbe and Juliets House. It suits first-time visitors and couples who want landmarks, dining and shopping at their doorstep, though prices and crowds run high.

Veronetta is the bohemian, student-heavy quarter across the Adige river, filled with the university, cheap trattorias, ethnic eateries and lively cheap bars. It appeals to younger travelers and budget-minded people who want an authentic, gritty and unpolished local scene rather than polished tourism.

San Zeno is a laid-back, characterful neighborhood built around its beautiful Romanesque basilica, with quiet cobbled streets, artisan workshops and neighborhood osterias. It suits travelers who want a residential, genuine Veronese feel while staying within walking distance of the center.

Borgo Trento is an elegant, leafy and affluent residential district just north of the river, known for its Liberty-style villas, parks and calm streets. It fits families and quieter visitors who prefer a refined, upscale and peaceful base away from tourist bustle.

Cittadella is a central, practical area between Porta Nuova station and Piazza Bra, mixing everyday shops, hotels and offices with easy transit access. It works well for business travelers and anyone who values convenient connections and walkability over historic charm.
lodging: Hotel Indigo Verona - Grand Hotel Des Arts

water.note: Tap water meets EU standards and is safe to drink.

transit.pay: A single urban ticket is EUR 1.50 (about USD 1.75) from tabaccherie, newsstands, ATV ticket offices or machines, or EUR 2.00 from the machine onboard; a day ticket is EUR 5 and covers one adult plus a child under 14. With ATV's Bip&Vai system you can simply tap a contactless bank card on the onboard validator, or buy via the Ticket Bus Verona app. Validate paper tickets every time you board.
transit.hours: Daytime buses run roughly 5:30am to 8:30-9pm; a reduced evening network of 'serale' lines runs until around midnight, with thinner service on Sundays and holidays.

transit.m: ATV Aerobus/Airlink shuttle to Porta Nuova station, ~15 min

places.name: Osteria al Duca

places.name: Trattoria Tre Marchetti

places.name: Alcova del Frate

places.name: Osteria Macafame

places.name: Antica Bottega del Vino

places.name: Trattoria Tre Marchetti

food.name: Pandoro
food.desc: Verona's star-shaped Christmas cake, invented here in 1894: tall, golden, egg-rich and dusted with vanilla sugar.

places.name: Pasticceria Flego
places.note: Verona pastry house with a strong local following for its cakes and pandoro.

places.name: Pasticceria De Rossi
places.note: Historic city-centre bakery, a long-standing stop for pandoro and morning pastries.

places.name: Caffe Borsari

food.name: Amarone and Valpolicella

places.name: Osteria del Bugiardo

places.name: Enoteca Segreta

food.name: Spritz
food.desc: Veneto aperitivo of prosecco, soda and Aperol or the more bitter Select, poured from late afternoon with crisps and olives.

places.name: Caffe Monte Baldo

places.name: Bars on Piazza delle Erbe
places.note: Terraces on the old market square, the postcard spot for an evening spritz.

places.name: Osteria del Bugiardo
places.note: Locals' choice for wine or spritz before dinner in the old town.

landmarks: Verona Arena
A remarkably preserved 1st-century Roman amphitheater still used for opera, its massive pink-marble tiers dominate Piazza Bra.
Casa di Giulietta (Juliet's House)
The famed balcony courtyard linked to Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, a must-photograph pilgrimage site for romantics.
Ponte Pietra
A graceful Roman stone bridge over the Adige River framed beautifully by the hillside church of San Giorgio in Braida.
Piazza delle Erbe
Verona's lively old Roman forum turned market square, ringed by colorful frescoed palazzi and a central fountain.
Castelvecchio
A crenellated medieval castle and museum on the Adige, notable for its Carlo Scarpa-redesigned galleries and fortified bridge.
Verona Cathedral (Duomo)
A Romanesque-Gothic cathedral with an ornately carved main portal, home to Titian's Assumption of the Virgin.
Torre dei Lamberti
Verona's tallest medieval tower, offering sweeping panoramic photos of the city's terracotta rooftops from its summit.
Ponte Scaligero
A fortified brick medieval bridge attached to Castelvecchio, striking for its crenellated arches spanning the Adige.
Basilica di San Zeno Maggiore
A masterpiece of Romanesque architecture featuring a rose window and famous bronze relief doors.
Piazza Bra
Verona's grand central square, lined with cafes and the elegant Liston promenade, with the Arena as its backdrop.

train.note: Verona Porta Nuova sits on the Brenner main line. Direct daytime Railjet/EuroCity trains run to Innsbruck and Munich; the Munich-Rome ÖBB Nightjet calls at Verona overnight. The Vienna-Milan Nightjet that also passes through Verona is currently suspended, so check before relying on it.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the Verona Porta Nuova bus terminal beside the station. FlixBus is the main international operator.

ferry.note: Verona has no sea ferries. Nearby Lake Garda (about 30 min away at Peschiera/Desenzano) has scenic passenger boats run by Navigazione Laghi, but these are domestic lake services only.

half.name: Venice
half.blurb: The floating city enchants with canals, gondolas, ornate palaces and the grand Piazza San Marco.

half.name: Lake Garda
half.blurb: Italy's largest lake dazzles with turquoise waters, lakeside villages, castles and scenic mountain backdrops.

half.name: Bologna
half.blurb: A lively university city famous for porticoed streets, medieval towers and celebrated regional cuisine.

half.name: Padua
half.blurb: An elegant old city known for frescoed chapels, arcaded squares and one of Europe's oldest universities.

half.name: Vicenza
half.blurb: A refined Renaissance city celebrated for graceful Palladian villas, palaces and its splendid classical theatre.

half.name: Mantua
half.blurb: A serene lake-ringed Renaissance town rich with ducal palaces, frescoes and quiet atmospheric piazzas.
